name: Does replacing foggy glass improve my home's energy efficiency?

mainEntity.name: Does replacing foggy glass improve my home's energy efficiency?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, replacing foggy glass significantly improves your home's energy efficiency. The fog indicates a failed seal in your insulated glass unit (IGU), meaning the inert gas (like argon) has escaped, and its insulating properties are lost. A new IGU restores this thermal barrier, reducing heat transfer into and out of your home. Opting for modern, energy-efficient glass types like Low-E (low-emissivity) glass can further enhance performance, leading to more stable indoor temperatures and potential savings on your utility bills.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, replacing foggy glass restores the insulating barrier of your windows, improving energy efficiency and potentially lowering utility costs, especially with Low-E glass.
